questions.q: What makes a brand successful, according to Klein?
a: Being seen as cool rather than making the best product
Offering the lowest price in its category
Manufacturing everything in its home country
Avoiding advertising and relying on quality
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the most successful brands sell an image and values, not necessarily the highest-quality product.

questions.q: Where do multinationals build factories to cut labor costs?
a: In export processing zones with few labor laws
In Western cities with strong unions
In countries with high minimum wages
In their own headquarters countries
questions.why: Lesson 2 says export processing zones suspend taxes and lack minimum wage or labor protections.

questions.q: What is a McJob, as described in the summary?
a: Part-time, minimum-wage service work
A management role in a fast-food chain
A unionized factory position
A temporary job for students only
questions.why: Lesson 2 says manufacturing jobs were replaced by part-time, minimum-wage service work known as McJobs.

questions.q: How can activists damage a brand, according to the summary?
a: By tying criticisms to the brand's name and image
By buying up all of its shares
By suing it in international courts
By ignoring it until it changes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says campaigns gain power when connected to a specific brand, letting consumers boycott it.

Creating a new brand to compete with a giant

Writing letters to company executives
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines culture jamming as using a brand's own ads against it, changing a slogan or image.
